My advice is to look closely at the land you're purchasing. Don't rely on a real estate agent. Whatever it takes you need to pull the title yourself and every single document referenced. Make sure you own the mineral rights and there are no other easements like this on your land. Don't try to get "more land" by accepting things like mineral easements. If you're trying to build something long term possibly multi-generational you don't want anyone else to have any claims. Since you're looking at multiple states check any "homestead" laws and protections. Homestead exemptions, etc in terms of debt collections.

You don't need AC. If you can't accept that then you're likely going to have a hell of a time homesteading. It is hard work and the kind of person who needs AC or has anyone in their family who needs AC is setting themselves up for a lot of pain.

Build the house yourself. It's not that difficult especially if you've got multiple people involved. Build a large garage with a studio type thing to start. I built my house first and I still regret not building a smaller guest type house first. You can find great deals on construction supplies if you have somewhere to store them until you need it. Similarly living on the land in a trailer, etc is a fucking nightmare depending on location. Also once you're sick of living like you're camping you will want to move into your house the second you can. That is a big mistake because it's going to make finishing construction 10x harder and longer as you deal with balancing a construction and living site in the same building.
Building a house is very difficult. Years, even with help, which you will definitely need for things like pouring a foundation, putting up roof joists, and so on.

There are a couple of hvac options. One is to bury large diameter corrugated pipe and use low com fans to pump air through them. As the air slowly moves through the pipe, it cools. You will need condensate pumps and filters for the pipe. You will want a thermal chimney as well. The hot air will exhaust through the chimney and coil air comes in from ground cooled air. Thermal chimneys will also move air on their own. With good insulation, infrared control on windows and these two types of air movement, you won’t get cooling like a traditional split system, but it will go a long ways toward comfort.
